label: github security advisory fix, a pull request on its temporary fork
title: {org}/{repo} GHSA-{ghsa} PR {pr}
prompt: Review security advisory GHSA-{ghsa} in {org}/{repo}. The proposed fix is pull request {pr} on the advisory's temporary private fork ({url}). Read the change locally: a fine-grained token cannot resolve a <repo>-ghsa-* fork and the API will 404. Assess whether the fix fully closes the vulnerability and whether any code path it should cover is missed. Propose findings before changing anything.
notes: Asked before the pull request row, which would take <repo>-ghsa-<id> for a repo of its own. The fork is the base repo plus a fix, so the worktree is the base repo's, named advisory-<id>-pr<num> as gwt names it. Not tagged pull-request, and the number is captured as pr rather than num: the pull request is on the fork, so a key naming the base repo would name somebody else's pull request or issue.

label: github security advisory fix, a branch on its temporary fork
title: {org}/{repo} GHSA-{ghsa} {ref}
prompt: Review security advisory GHSA-{ghsa} in {org}/{repo}. The proposed fix is branch {ref} on the advisory's temporary private fork ({url}), and its tip commit is the fix. Read the change locally: a fine-grained token cannot resolve a <repo>-ghsa-* fork and the API will 404. Assess whether the fix fully closes the vulnerability and whether any code path it should cover is missed. Propose findings before changing anything.
notes: Asked before the branch row, which would take <repo>-ghsa-<id> for a repo of its own. The worktree is the base repo's, advisory-<id>, on the fork's fix branch, as gwt lays it.

label: github security advisory
title: {org}/{repo} {ghsa}
prompt: Investigate security advisory {ghsa} in {org}/{repo} ({url}). Try to read it with gh api repos/{org}/{repo}/security-advisories/{ghsa}. If the token cannot (a draft needs a classic token with repo admin), ask me to paste it. Propose a fix plan before changing anything.
notes: The advisory page. The worktree is advisory-<GHSA id> off the default branch, as gwt names it: the local fix branch you would open a pull request from.

label: github pull request
title: {org}/{repo}#{num} {title}
prompt:
Review the pull request at {url}.

The worktree is already on its branch. Read the diff against the base branch first, then the description, then the discussion. Report what you would block on and what is only a preference.
notes: A trailing path, query or fragment is allowed on purpose. .../pull/5/files and .../pull/5 are the same pull request. A path in front of /pull, or letters glued to the number, is not a pull request and does not match.

label: github issue
title: {org}/{repo}#{num} {title}
notes: An issue has no branch of its own, so the branch is named for the issue and the worktree is one you make before starting.

label: github branch
title: {org}/{repo} {ref}
prompt:
Continue the work on branch {ref} of {org}/{repo} ({url}).

Read the log against the default branch first, then say what the branch is doing and what looks unfinished.
notes: A tree url can also carry a folder after the branch, and the url alone cannot say where the branch name stops. The whole tail is taken as the branch, so paste the branch page, not a folder in it. Every segment starts with a letter, digit, _ or -, so no segment is . or .. and the worktree path cannot climb out.

label: a repository on github
title: {org}/{repo}
notes: THE SHRUG, and it belongs at the bottom. A url on a host we know that matches nothing more specific still gets a dialog, pointed at the clone. Refusing would be correct and useless. A clone url's .git is not part of the repo's name, as gwt reads it.
